name: 稳定二叉树的最小操作次数
englishName: Minimum Operations to Stabilize a Binary Tree
hints: Try using tree DP. Let dp[u](x) represent the minimum number of operations needed to make the subtree rooted at u stable, assuming the final value of node u is x.

If node u has a child v, the final value of v must differ from x by at most 1. Therefore, the contribution of this child is min(dp[v](x - 1), dp[v](x), dp[v](x + 1)). How can you combine the contributions of all children?

Computing the DP for every possible value of x would be too expensive. Observe that each DP function is convex and piecewise linear. Can you represent such a function efficiently using its breakpoints instead of storing all its values?

Consider how taking the minimum over [x - 1, x + 1] changes the breakpoints of a convex function. Use an efficient data structure to maintain these breakpoints and merge the functions of different subtrees.
